claims.quote: Short (< 120 ms): WPW, LGL, junctional rhythm

claims.text: Aspects (abnormal in red) Rhythm in junctional rhythm: regular, narrow-complex, arising from the AV node
claims.quote: Junctional rhythms are narrow complex, regular rhythms arising from the AV node.
Short (< 120 ms): WPW, LGL, junctional rhythm
The features of Lown-Ganong-Levine syndrome LGL syndrome are a very short PR interval with normal P waves and QRS complexes and absent delta waves.

claims.text: P waves in junctional rhythm: absent or abnormal (e.g., inverted, retrograde)
claims.quote: P waves are either absent or abnormal (e.g. inverted) with a short PR interval (=retrograde P waves).

claims.text: QRS in WPW: delta wave (slurred, slow rise of the first part of the QRS) and QRS > 110 ms
claims.quote: PR interval < 120ms Delta wave: slurring slow rise of initial portion of the QRS QRS prolongation > 110ms
claims.locator: ECG features of WPW in sinus rhythm

claims.text: QRS in LGL: normal, with no delta wave
claims.quote: The features of Lown-Ganong-Levine syndrome LGL syndrome are a very short PR interval with normal P waves and QRS complexes and absent delta waves.

claims.text: ST and T in WPW: discordant — opposite in direction to the main QRS deflection
claims.quote: Discordant ST-segment and T-wave changes (i.e. in the opposite direction to the major component of the QRS complex)
claims.locator: ECG features of WPW in sinus rhythm

claims.text: Causes (mechanism and diagnoses) Diagnoses: pre-excitation syndromes (WPW, LGL) or AV nodal (junctional) rhythm
claims.quote: A short PR interval is seen with: Preexcitation syndromes AV nodal (junctional) rhythm.

claims.text: Mechanism (pre-excitation): an accessory pathway conducts faster than normal, giving the short PR, and also forms a re-entry circuit for tachyarrhythmias
claims.quote: The accessory pathway conducts impulses faster than normal, producing a short PR interval. The accessory pathway also acts as an anatomical re-entry circuit, making patients susceptible to re-entry tachyarrhythmias.

claims.text: LGL's existence is disputed; the term should not be used without paroxysmal tachycardia
claims.quote: The term should not be used in the absence of paroxysmal tachycardia. Existence is disputed.

claims.text: Symptoms Pre-excitation: episodes of paroxysmal SVT, specifically AV re-entry tachycardia (AVRT)
claims.quote: Patients present with episodes of paroxsymal supraventricular tachycardia (SVT), specifically atrioventricular re-entry tachycardia (AVRT)

claims.text: WPW carries a small risk of sudden cardiac death
claims.quote: Associated with a small risk of sudden cardiac death

claims.text: Treatment WPW: acutely, treat the presenting arrhythmia; long term, antiarrhythmics or ablation of the accessory pathway (details under Arrhythmias › WPW)
claims.quote: Acute: treatment of the presenting arrhythmia Long-term: chronic antiarrhythmic therapy for arrhythmia prevention or ablation of the accessory AV connection
